task: Address three improvements to the in-browser code editor (CodeMirror 6) in the leetlab Vite/React client-only SPA: (1) add code folding of blocks/functions/objects (fold gutter + foldable ranges) for JS and TS modes; (2) optimize autocomplete — the synchronous scopeCompletionSource(globalThis) runs heavy work on every keystroke (typing tick) and causes input lag; move it off the typing tick via caching/deferral; (3) after each run dispatched by EditorPane.handleRun, auto-emit console.log(`${counter}`, result) with a monotonically increasing per-session run counter and the run result. A previously listed 4th item ('TS/linter not working when deployed') was investigated by the user and is a false alarm, out of scope. Quality bar: prototype / best-effort.

analysis.objective: Deliver three prototype-level improvements to the CodeMirror 6 editor in the leetlab client-only SPA: code folding, a non-blocking autocomplete pipeline, and an automatic per-run console.log of the run counter and result.
analysis.successDefinition: In a local dev build: (1) the editor shows a fold gutter and folds/unfolds foldable syntactic ranges (blocks, functions, objects) for both JS and TS modes via gutter click and fold keybindings; (2) typing quickly in a large document no longer blocks keystrokes on completion computation — completion work is moved off the typing tick and the dropdown still produces scope/service/(TS) built-in completions when the user pauses; (3) after every code run triggered from EditorPane.handleRun (run and submit, success and handled-error paths), exactly one console.log(`${counter}`, result) is emitted where counter is a monotonically increasing run number starting at 1 and result is the run's outcome value; the app still typechecks (tsc) and builds (vite build), with light manual verification only and no required new automated tests.
assumptions: 'result' in item 3 means the run's aggregated outcome available in handleRun — the LastRun summary object (results array plus verdict/passed/total) or the results array; exact shape is implementer's choice as long as it is the run's result data.
The run counter is per-session/in-memory (a module-level counter that resets on page reload); no persistence across reloads is required.

The counter increments once per handleRun invocation that actually dispatches a run to the sandbox worker, and the log fires once per such run including runs that end in Wrong Answer, TLE, or sandbox compile error; runs aborted before execution (TS compile error, no valid testcases, busy) need not log.
@codemirror/language (installed) supplies foldGutter/codeFolding/foldKeymap and the javascript language package provides foldable ranges; no new fold-range parser is needed.
Folding state does not need to be persisted between sessions or mounts.
'Optimize autocomplete' is satisfied by demonstrably removing the synchronous per-keystroke cost; a formal latency benchmark is not required at the prototype bar.
The existing single EditorView architecture in CodeEditor.tsx is kept; changes are additive extensions plus a completion-source wrapper.
The console.log uses a template literal for the counter exactly as specified (`${counter}`), producing a string first argument.
Existing completion behavior/quality (which items appear) should be preserved as closely as practical; minor ordering or timing changes are acceptable.
risks: Moving the TypeScript LanguageService completion source into a Web Worker may be large: the CDN TS compiler/libs, VFS, and getCompletionEntryDetails calls would all need to run worker-side, risking scope creep beyond the prototype bar.
The TS built-in completion source is already async and CDN-gated; if the real lag source is not scopeCompletionSource(globalThis), the fix must target the actual source.
CodeMirror completion sources must return synchronously-scheduled promises; an incorrectly wrapped async/cached source can break the dropdown, validFor stickiness, or cause flicker.
foldGutter added without matching theme/CSS may render poorly against the existing custom editor theme.
Determining the correct single insertion point for the run log across the success, timeout, compile-failure, and generic-catch branches of handleRun risks double-logging or missing paths.
The counter living in React component state could reset on remount or double-fire under StrictMode double-invoke; a module-level counter avoids this but must be chosen deliberately.
Worker bundling that works in `vite dev` but fails or 404s in the hashed static surge.sh build would pass local checks yet break deployment.
'result' being interpreted differently than the user intended (e.g. logging the raw worker payload vs. the processed verdict object) could require rework.
outOfScope: Item 4 / the 'TS or linter not working when deployed' report — user confirmed it is a false alarm and explicitly excluded.
Wiring @codemirror/lint diagnostics or a linter into the editor — installed but not part of these three improvements.
Rewriting or relocating the TypeScript compile step (tsCompiler.compile) or the sandbox.worker.ts run pipeline beyond adding the log — the run mechanism itself is not being changed.
Persisting fold state, editor preferences, or the run counter to localStorage / app store — prototype scope is in-memory only.
Adding a visible in-app run-counter or run-history UI — item 3 targets the browser console only, not the results panel.
Piping sandbox user-code console.log output into the browser console or a custom console panel — item 3 is about the host app logging run metadata, not surfacing sandbox logs.
A formal performance benchmark harness or profiling report for autocomplete latency — light verification only at the prototype bar.
New automated test suites for folding, the completion wrapper, or the run log — user marked tests optional.
Broader editor features (multi-cursor config, minimap, bracket-pair colorization, search panel, linting gutter) not named in the three items.
Refactoring CodeEditor.tsx's ~881-line structure or splitting the component beyond what the autocomplete change requires.
Changing completion content/ranking quality or adding new completion sources — only the execution model is being optimized.
Upgrading CodeMirror or related package versions.
analysis.domainShapeReason: The task is entirely about editor machinery — CodeMirror extensions, a completion computation pipeline, caching/deferral plumbing, and a console diagnostic — with no business entities, rules, or workflows involved.

ubiquitousLanguage.meaning: The CodeMirror gutter column (from @codemirror/language) showing fold/unfold toggles next to foldable ranges.
A syntactic region (block, function body, object literal) the language package marks as collapsible.
A function registered via javascriptLanguage.data.of({autocomplete}) that returns completion candidates for the current cursor context; today: scope, sandbox-service, and TS built-in sources.
The synchronous keystroke event cycle that must stay unblocked; completion work currently runs on it and causes input lag.
The mechanism (cache, debounce, deferral, or worker) that moves completion computation off the typing tick.
The autocompletion() option (currently 350ms) controlling how long the user must pause before the dropdown opens.
One execution of the user's code dispatched by EditorPane.handleRun to a fresh sandbox.worker.ts instance (6s timeout), covering both Run and Submit.
A monotonically increasing per-session integer (starting at 1) identifying which run number the current run is; logged as the first console.log argument.
The run's outcome value passed as the second console.log argument — the LastRun summary (results/verdict/passed/total) or the results array.

discoveryFindings.finding: extensionsFor(lang) in src/components/CodeEditor.tsx builds a hand-picked flat array (no basicSetup): javascript() language, ...editorCompletionSources(lang), autocompletion({activateOnTypingDelay:350}), closeBrackets(), history(), a single keymap.of([...toggleComment, indentWithTab, closeBracketsKeymap, completionKeymap, defaultKeymap, historyKeymap]), an updateListener, editorTheme, syntaxHighlighting, lintGutter(), tsLint|syntaxLint, plus usage-template popover extensions.
discoveryFindings.implication: Folding is added as explicit extensions: import foldGutter/codeFolding/foldKeymap from @codemirror/language, add codeFolding()+foldGutter() to the array, merge ...foldKeymap into the existing keymap.of([]). No basicSetup to toggle.

discoveryFindings.finding: No fold references anywhere in src. @codemirror/language@6.12.4 exports codeFolding, foldGutter, foldKeymap, foldable. @codemirror/lang-javascript provides foldable ranges via the Lezer grammar for both js and ts modes.
discoveryFindings.implication: Item 1 is a pure additive change; foldable ranges work out of the box for JS and TS. Reconfigure rebuilds the extension list per language so fold extensions just go in extensionsFor().

discoveryFindings.area: Editor theme / CSS for fold gutter
discoveryFindings.finding: editorTheme is a large EditorView.theme({}) with custom .cm-gutters, .cm-lineNumbers, .cm-activeLineGutter styling. No .cm-foldGutter / .cm-foldPlaceholder rules.
discoveryFindings.implication: foldGutter() inherits .cm-gutters chrome but default markers may be low-contrast on the dark theme; add .cm-foldGutter and .cm-foldPlaceholder rules to editorTheme.

discoveryFindings.finding: Language switch dispatches StateEffect.reconfigure.of(extensionsFor(lang)) with an external annotation; full extension list rebuilt each switch, no Compartment. Initial mount also calls extensionsFor(st.lang).
discoveryFindings.implication: New fold/autocomplete extensions in extensionsFor() apply automatically on mount and language switch; fold state is lost on switch (acceptable per assumptions).

discoveryFindings.finding: editorCompletionSources(lang) registers 3 separate javascriptLanguage.data.of({autocomplete}) entries: (1) scopeCompletionSource(globalThis) — SYNC, walks the real global object graph on every call with no memoization; (2) sandboxServiceCompletions — SYNC but cheap (DATA precomputed once at module load); (3) builtInTsCompletion (ts only) — ASYNC, already defers via setTimeout(0) and checks context.aborted.
discoveryFindings.implication: The TS source is already off the typing tick. The remaining synchronous per-keystroke cost is scopeCompletionSource(globalThis). Item 2 wraps/replaces that source with a cached/deferred equivalent, not a TS worker.

discoveryFindings.finding: scopeCompletionSource(globalThis) is CodeMirror's built-in; it enumerates properties of globalThis and nested objects synchronously each invocation with no memoization. autocompletion() is configured only with activateOnTypingDelay:350.
discoveryFindings.implication: Confirmed likely primary lag source. Cheapest fix: memoize the global-scope completion list (compute once), serve from cache with validFor; or defer via setTimeout(0). No worker needed.

discoveryFindings.finding: Only one worker: src/infrastructure/sandbox.worker.ts, imported in useRunCode.ts as `import SandboxWorker from '@infra/sandbox.worker?worker'` then `new SandboxWorker()`; vite.config.ts sets worker:{format:'es'}. tsCompiler.ts/tsCheck.ts do NOT use a worker — they load TS from CDN on the main thread.
discoveryFindings.implication: If a worker were needed, the pattern is a dedicated *.worker.ts file with the ?worker query. A worker for completions is overkill given the scope-source finding.

discoveryFindings.finding: handleRun(isSubmit) branches: (A) early return if busy. (B) ts compile error from tsCompiler.compile -> setLastRun verdict 'Compile Error', return (do NOT log). (C) !runnable.length -> alert('No valid testcases'), return (do NOT log). (D) success: `const {results,logs} = await run(...)`, computes passed/total/ms/verdict, setLastRun({results,logs,verdict,passed,total,ms}). (E) catch err.type==='timeout': tleResults, verdict 'Time Limit Exceeded', setLastRun. (F) catch err.type==='compile' (sandbox): setLastRun verdict 'Compile Error'. (G) catch else: console.error(e)+alert. finally: setBusy(false).
discoveryFindings.implication: The log should fire once for any run actually dispatched to the sandbox worker: paths D, E, F. Cleanest: a helper logRun(result) called at each of the 3 setLastRun sites; log the same LastRun-summary object passed to setLastRun.

discoveryFindings.finding: handleRun is a component method invoked only by button onClick, not in an effect, so StrictMode effect double-invoke does not double-call it. EditorPane holds only useState(busy/fmt) and useRef(fmtTimer); no existing counter.
discoveryFindings.implication: A module-level `let runCounter = 0` incremented inside handleRun is safe and survives re-renders/remounts within a session; a useRef would reset on remount. Module-level recommended.

discoveryFindings.finding: run(code, problem, cases) returns Promise<{results: LastRunCase[]; logs: Array<{l:string;t:string}>}>. On timeout rejects {type:'timeout', results: partial, logs}; sandbox compile rejects {type:'compile', error, logs}. run() also already forwards sandbox user console.log to the real browser console during the run.
discoveryFindings.implication: Natural 'result' for item 3's second arg is the derived LastRun summary EditorPane builds. Item 3's host-metadata log is distinct from the sandbox console forwarding and must not be confused with it (out of scope to change).

discoveryFindings.finding: docs/roadmaps has only this task's .tmp analysis; no other roadmap touches fold/autocomplete/logging. Existing console usage: useRunCode forwards sandbox console msgs; EditorPane catch-all does console.error(e). No per-run metadata logging exists.
discoveryFindings.implication: No prior art to reconcile; all three items are greenfield additive changes.

discoveryFindings.finding: @codemirror/language@6.12.4 exports codeFolding, foldGutter, foldKeymap, foldable, syntaxHighlighting, syntaxTree. @codemirror/lint@6.9.7 already wired (linter + lintGutter) but out of scope. @codemirror/autocomplete@6.20.3 supports activateOnTypingDelay.
discoveryFindings.implication: All fold primitives for item 1 are available at the installed version; no dependency bump required.

phases.name: Add fold gutter and style it for the dark theme
phases.goal: The CodeMirror editor shows a clickable fold gutter that collapses/expands foldable syntactic ranges (blocks, function bodies, object literals) in both JS and TS modes via gutter click and fold keybindings, and the fold toggles plus the collapsed-region placeholder are legible against the editor's existing dark custom theme.
phases.rationale: The code editor currently has no way to collapse sections of code, so long solutions are hard to navigate. CodeMirror's language package can already detect foldable regions from the JavaScript/TypeScript grammar; the editor just never enabled the feature. A 'fold gutter' is the narrow column beside the line numbers showing a triangle/arrow toggle next to each collapsible region. Because the editor uses a hand-written dark color theme, CodeMirror's default fold markers and the '…' placeholder shown for collapsed code would be near-invisible without matching CSS, so enabling and styling folding is one small piece of work in one file.
changes: Import codeFolding, foldGutter and foldKeymap from @codemirror/language.
In extensionsFor(lang), add codeFolding() and foldGutter() to the extension array near the other gutter extensions.
Merge ...foldKeymap into the existing single keymap.of([...]) binding list so fold/unfold keyboard shortcuts work.

In the editorTheme EditorView.theme({...}) object, add .cm-foldGutter .cm-gutterElement rules (toggle color, cursor, hover) consistent with the existing .cm-gutters / .cm-activeLineGutter colors, and a .cm-foldPlaceholder rule (background, border, text color, padding) so collapsed regions read as a distinct pill.

Manually verify in a dev build that both the JS and TS starter templates show fold toggles, that clicking one collapses a function/block and expanding restores it, and that toggles and placeholder are readable at rest and on hover.
inputs: src/components/CodeEditor.tsx extensionsFor(lang) assembly and the editorTheme object
CodeMirror 6 code-folding API reference (composition of codeFolding/foldGutter, foldKeymap bindings, .cm-foldGutter/.cm-foldPlaceholder/.cm-gutterElement class names)
phases.expectedResult: extensionsFor(lang) includes codeFolding() + foldGutter() with foldKeymap in the keymap, and editorTheme contains .cm-foldGutter and .cm-foldPlaceholder rules, so the editor folds/unfolds ranges legibly in JS and TS modes.
phases.compensation: Remove the codeFolding()/foldGutter() entries, the ...foldKeymap spread, and the added .cm-foldGutter/.cm-foldPlaceholder theme rules from CodeEditor.tsx; no persisted state to clean up.

rubric.label: Fold extensions present in editor config
rubric.ruleStatement: The compiled editor extension array for each language mode must include CodeMirror's code-folding and fold-gutter extensions plus the fold keymap, sourced from @codemirror/language.
passCriteria: In src/components/CodeEditor.tsx, codeFolding and foldGutter are imported from "@codemirror/language" (not stubbed or re-implemented locally)
The value returned by extensionsFor(lang) contains a call to codeFolding() and a call to foldGutter() for both js and ts modes
foldKeymap (imported from @codemirror/language) is spread into an existing keymap.of([...]) call, not passed as a bare array
Running npm run build succeeds with these imports
failureExamples: foldGutter() added only for JS, TS branch left unchanged
codeFolding() imported but never added to the extension list
foldKeymap passed as keymap.of(foldKeymap) at top level instead of merged into the existing keymap array
Old v5-style import path used and build fails

rubric.label: Folding actually collapses and restores ranges at runtime
rubric.ruleStatement: In a running dev build, clicking a fold toggle in the gutter collapses the corresponding syntactic range and clicking again restores the exact original text, in both JS and TS modes.
passCriteria: Open the editor with a JS snippet containing a multi-line function body and a multi-line object literal; a fold marker is visible in the gutter next to each foldable range's opening line
Clicking the marker on the function replaces its body with a single placeholder and reduces visible line count; clicking again returns the buffer to byte-identical original content
Repeat the check in TypeScript mode with a snippet containing an interface or class body
The fold keybinding folds/unfolds the block containing the cursor
failureExamples: Gutter shows markers but clicking does nothing
Fold works in JS but TS mode shows no markers
Unfolding leaves a stray placeholder character or loses indentation
Keybinding does nothing because foldKeymap was not merged

rubric.label: Fold toggles and placeholder are legible on the dark theme
rubric.ruleStatement: editorTheme defines explicit rules for the fold gutter elements and the collapsed-region placeholder that render with sufficient contrast against the editor's existing dark background.
passCriteria: editorTheme in CodeEditor.tsx contains selectors for .cm-foldGutter (or .cm-foldGutter .cm-gutterElement) and .cm-foldPlaceholder
The .cm-foldPlaceholder rule sets both a color and a background/border differing from the editor background color used elsewhere in editorTheme
In the running dark editor the fold arrows are distinguishable from the gutter background and the placeholder (…) is readable, not dark-on-dark
Removing the new rules makes the markers hard to see (i.e. they are not relying on default light-theme styles)
failureExamples: Placeholder renders as default black text on the dark editor background
Fold arrows present but same color as gutter, effectively invisible
Styles added to a global CSS file instead of editorTheme
Only .cm-foldPlaceholder styled, fold gutter markers left at default

rubric.label: Change fits the existing extension/theme composition
rubric.ruleStatement: The new folding wiring reuses the file's existing patterns for assembling extensions, keymaps, and theme rules rather than introducing a parallel mechanism.
passCriteria: Fold extensions are added inside the same extensionsFor(lang) function/array that already returns the other language extensions, in the same style
The keymap change modifies the single existing keymap.of([...]) call; no second keymap.of or EditorView instance is introduced
Fold theme rules are added as additional keys in the existing editorTheme object literal, matching its style
git diff for the phase touches only src/components/CodeEditor.tsx and shows additions, not restructuring of unrelated setup
failureExamples: A new buildFoldingExtensions() helper created alongside extensionsFor
Second EditorState.create or compartment introduced just for folding
Fold styles placed in a new EditorView.theme() call, creating two theme layers
Diff reformats or reorders the whole extensions array

rubric.label: Existing editor features still work
rubric.ruleStatement: Adding the fold gutter does not break existing gutters, keybindings, language switching, or the editor's controlled value flow.
passCriteria: Line-number gutter still renders and aligns with content after the fold gutter is added
Pre-existing keybindings (indent, comment toggle, history undo/redo) still fire — spot-check at least two
Switching language between JS and TS at runtime does not throw and folding continues to work after the switch
The editor's value binding still reflects edits (type a character, confirm store updates)
npm test passes, or if no tests cover the editor, the build and a manual smoke test show no console errors on mount
failureExamples: foldKeymap ordering shadows an existing binding
Language switch now throws
Line numbers misalign because fold gutter CSS sets a conflicting line-height
Console error 'Unrecognized extension value' on mount

phases.healerHint: Most likely failure: foldGutter() is wired into only one language branch (or added after the language extension so TS shows no markers) — fastest fix is to add codeFolding() + foldGutter() once in the shared part of extensionsFor(lang) so both JS and TS inherit it.

phases.name: Cache global-scope completions off the typing tick
phases.goal: The scope completion source no longer walks the live globalThis object graph synchronously on every keystroke; instead it serves candidates from a memoized list so fast typing in a large document is not blocked by completion computation.
phases.rationale: An autocomplete 'completion source' is a function CodeMirror calls to get dropdown suggestions for the cursor position. One of the three registered sources, scopeCompletionSource(globalThis), enumerates every property of the browser's global object and nested objects on each call with no caching, and this synchronous work runs on the 'typing tick' — the keystroke event cycle that must stay fast — causing input lag. The other two sources are already cheap or already async, so only this one needs fixing. A Web Worker for TypeScript completions would be large and is out of scope; caching/deferral is the prototype-appropriate fix.
changes: Wrap scopeCompletionSource(globalThis) so the expensive global-scope candidate list is computed at most once (lazily on first use, or on an idle/debounce timer) and reused across keystrokes for the session.
Have the wrapped source return a CompletionResult with an appropriate validFor regexp so CodeMirror reuses results while the user keeps typing an identifier instead of recomputing.
Ensure the wrapped source still honors context.aborted and returns null when there is no word to complete, matching the existing sources' contract.
Manually verify that pausing after typing an identifier prefix still shows global/scope completions, and that rapid typing in a large solution no longer stutters.
inputs: CodeMirror autocomplete completion-source contract (CompletionResult, validFor, context.aborted)
phases.expectedResult: editorCompletions.ts registers a memoized/deferred replacement for the raw scopeCompletionSource(globalThis) that computes the global-scope list once and serves it via validFor.
phases.compensation: Restore the direct javascriptLanguage.data.of({autocomplete: scopeCompletionSource(globalThis)}) registration and delete the wrapper.

rubric.label: Global-scope list computed once, not per typing tick
rubric.ruleStatement: The deliverable must compute the globalThis-derived candidate list at most once and reuse it across subsequent completion invocations rather than calling the raw scopeCompletionSource(globalThis) synchronously on every call.
passCriteria: In src/infrastructure/editorCompletions.ts there is a module-level variable (or closure) holding the cached candidate list / cached CompletionResult, assigned exactly once behind an `if (cache == null)` style guard or a lazy singleton
The raw scopeCompletionSource / globalThis object-graph walk is invoked from inside that guarded block only, not on the hot path of the exported completion source function
Adding a temporary console.count inside the guarded block and typing 20+ identifier characters logs it once (or zero until first trigger), not once per keystroke
Every `scopeCompletionSource(globalThis)` call site in the file is inside the memoization guard, not the returned function body
failureExamples: The exported source still calls scopeCompletionSource(globalThis)(context) directly on each invocation with only the result array cached afterward
A cache variable exists but is re-seeded every call because the guard checks the wrong variable
Memoization keyed on context or document text, so it recomputes on every edit

rubric.label: CompletionResult returns a validFor that covers identifier typing
rubric.ruleStatement: The returned CompletionResult must include a validFor (regexp or function) matching a contiguous identifier so CodeMirror filters the cached list locally while the user keeps typing instead of re-querying the source.
passCriteria: The returned object literal has a validFor property whose value is a RegExp matching JS identifier characters (e.g. /^[\w$]*$/) or a function returning boolean
`from` on the result is the start of the current word (e.g. from context.matchBefore(/[\w$]+/)), not a hardcoded context.pos
In the running editor, trigger completion then type 3 more identifier characters without pausing: the dropdown narrows/filters live and does not close or flash empty
After the first trigger, typing more identifier chars does not re-enter the exported source function until a non-identifier char or a new word
failureExamples: Result omits validFor, so CodeMirror calls the source again on every keystroke
validFor: /.*/ or a regexp matching whitespace/dots, causing stale results across word boundaries
`from` is context.pos so options are inserted without replacing the typed prefix

rubric.label: Honors aborted context and null word
rubric.ruleStatement: The completion source must return null when there is no word to complete and must respect context.aborted, so it never returns a populated result for a stale or cancelled request.
passCriteria: The function computes a word match and returns null when it is null and context.explicit is false
There is an explicit `if (context.aborted) return null` check before returning any result
Trigger completion in an empty document with no identifier typed and no explicit invocation: no dropdown appears
Type a space or punctuation then check the dropdown closes rather than showing global identifiers
failureExamples: Function always returns the cached result regardless of whether the cursor is on a word
No context.aborted check, so a result is returned for a superseded keystroke
Returns an empty-options result object instead of null, which suppresses other sources

rubric.label: Does not fight the editor's existing completion configuration
rubric.ruleStatement: The memoized source must be wired into the same completion sources list the editor already uses, preserving the other completion sources and the existing autocompletion config.
passCriteria: The new memoized source replaces the old scope source in the same editorCompletionSources array, at the same position
No second autocompletion(...) extension is added; the existing one is reused
The sandbox-service source and the TS built-in source are still registered after the change
In the running editor, a sandbox-service completion (e.g. one of the 5 service handles) still triggers and appears as before
activateOnTypingDelay and other autocompletion options are unchanged
failureExamples: A fresh autocompletion({override:[memoizedScopeSource]}) is appended, silently dropping the other sources
The memoized source is exported but never referenced by editorCompletionSources, so nothing changes at runtime
The change also flips activateOnTyping or bumps the delay

rubric.label: Same candidates still surface as before
rubric.ruleStatement: The memoized list must contain the same global-scope identifiers the raw scopeCompletionSource(globalThis) produced, so completion coverage does not regress.
passCriteria: Pick 3 known globals (Array, Object, Promise, console) and trigger completion for each prefix: each still appears in the dropdown
The memoized list length is within a small delta of scopeCompletionSource(globalThis)'s output captured once at init (not empty, not drastically smaller)
Selecting an option inserts the same text as before (labels/apply unchanged)
If the old source produced type/boost metadata on options, those fields are still present on the cached options
failureExamples: Cached list built by Object.keys(globalThis) directly, losing prototype-chain / nested members
Options lose their type icons or detail
Cache captured before app globals are attached, so app-level globals are missing

phases.healerHint: Most likely failure: results are memoized but the returned CompletionResult has no (or too-broad) validFor, so CodeMirror still re-invokes the source every keystroke and typing still stutters — fix by returning { from: word.from, options, validFor: /^[\w$]*$/ } with `from` at the identifier start.

phases.name: Log run counter and result after each run
phases.goal: Every code execution dispatched from EditorPane.handleRun (Run and Submit; success, timeout, and sandbox compile-error paths) emits exactly one console.log(`${counter}`, result) to the browser console, where counter is a per-session integer starting at 1 and incrementing once per dispatched run, and result is that run's LastRun summary.
phases.rationale: There is currently no way to see, from the browser console, how many runs happened this session or what each produced. This phase adds a lightweight diagnostic: after a run actually reaches the sandbox, log a monotonically increasing run number and the run's outcome object. Runs aborted before execution (TypeScript compile error, no valid testcases, editor busy) must not log or increment. A 'run' covers both the Run and Submit buttons; the 'run counter' is in-memory only and resets on page reload.
changes: Add a module-level `let runCounter = 0` in EditorPane.tsx (not component state or a ref, so it survives re-renders and StrictMode remounts).
Add a small helper logRun(result) that does `runCounter += 1; console.log(`${runCounter}`, result);`.

Call logRun with the same LastRun summary object at each of the three setLastRun sites that follow a dispatched run: the success path (D), the timeout catch (E), and the sandbox compile-error catch (F).
Do not call logRun on the early-return paths: busy (A), pre-run TS compile error (B), no valid testcases (C), or the generic catch/alert path (G).
Manually verify in a dev build that Run then Submit logs `1` then `2` with the result object, that a wrong-answer run still logs and increments, and that a pre-run TS compile error does not.
inputs: handleRun(isSubmit) branch structure in src/components/EditorPane.tsx (paths A–G)
the LastRun summary object passed to setLastRun (results/verdict/passed/total/ms/logs)
assumption: counter is in-memory per session, increments once per dispatched run
phases.expectedResult: handleRun calls a module-level-counter-backed logRun(result) at exactly the three post-dispatch setLastRun sites, emitting one console.log(`${counter}`, result) per run.
phases.compensation: Delete the module-level runCounter, the logRun helper, and its three call sites in EditorPane.tsx.

rubric.label: Exactly one log per dispatched run
rubric.ruleStatement: Each run that reaches dispatch emits exactly one console.log call, formatted as (`${counter}`, result).
passCriteria: Grep src/components/EditorPane.tsx for console.log — every occurrence is inside the single helper logRun (or there is exactly one console.log total)
In logRun, the console.log first argument is a string template of the counter, and the second argument is the result/LastRun summary object
In devtools Console, click Run once on a passing solution: exactly one new log line appears showing a number then the run-result object
Click Submit once immediately after: exactly one additional log line appears (total 2)
No run produces two entries for the same click
failureExamples: console.log placed inside a React render body or useEffect without guard, firing on every re-render
logRun called both at the setLastRun site and inside a shared finally block, producing two lines per run
console.log(runCounter, result) passing a number (not a string) as the first arg

rubric.label: Counter is monotonic and per-session
rubric.ruleStatement: The counter is a module-level integer starting at 1 on first logged run and increasing by exactly 1 for each subsequent dispatched run within the same page session.
passCriteria: `let runCounter = 0` (or equivalent) is declared at module scope in EditorPane.tsx, not inside the component, not in a useRef/useState
logRun increments before logging so the first logged value is 1
In the Console, performing Run, Submit, Run, Submit, Run logs first-args exactly 1,2,3,4,5 in order
A wrong-answer run still advances the counter by 1 (correctness does not gate the increment)
The counter never decreases or resets between runs without a full page reload; after a hard reload it restarts at 1
failureExamples: Counter stored in useState, so a re-render or remount resets it
Increment done as `runCounter + 1` without assignment
Counter incremented at dispatch but logged from a stale closure, producing 1,1,2,2

rubric.label: Success, timeout, and sandbox-compile branches all log
rubric.ruleStatement: logRun is invoked on each of the three post-dispatch outcome paths — success, timeout, and sandbox compile-error — with that path's LastRun summary.
passCriteria: In EditorPane.tsx, the three setLastRun calls that occur after a run has been dispatched (success, timeout, sandbox compile-error) each have an adjacent logRun call with the same summary passed to setLastRun
A passing solution logs a result object reflecting an accepted status
A solution with an infinite loop forces the timeout: Console shows exactly one log whose result reflects the timeout status
A solution with a syntax error that fails inside the sandbox (not the pre-run TS check): Console shows exactly one log reflecting the sandbox compile-error status
The object logged is the same LastRun summary shown in the UI results panel for that run
failureExamples: logRun added only to the success branch
logRun passed a hardcoded or empty object instead of the branch's actual summary
Timeout path calls setLastRun in a catch block that logRun was not added to

rubric.label: No log on pre-run abort paths
rubric.ruleStatement: Runs that early-return before dispatch — busy/in-flight, pre-run TypeScript compile failure, no testcases, and the generic catch — emit no log and do not advance the counter.
passCriteria: The early-return branches for busy (A), pre-run TS compile error (B), no testcases (C), and generic catch (G) contain no call to logRun and no console.log
Clicking Run twice rapidly so the second hits the busy guard produces only one log line
A TypeScript error caught by the pre-run check produces no log line, and the next successful run logs the previous counter value + 1
A problem/state with no testcases produces no log line
Total console.log count over a session equals the number of runs that actually dispatched, not the number of clicks
failureExamples: logRun placed at the top of handleRun before the guard checks
A shared finally block calls logRun even when the function returned early
Pre-run compile error increments the counter, so run numbering skips values

rubric.label: No double logging under React StrictMode
rubric.ruleStatement: A single user-initiated run produces exactly one log even when the app runs under React.StrictMode double-invocation in development.
passCriteria: logRun is called from the event-handler / async dispatch flow of handleRun, not from a useEffect, useMemo, or render body
In a dev build with StrictMode active, clicking Run once produces exactly one log line
Mounting/unmounting EditorPane (navigate away and back) without running produces no log lines
No console.log is reachable from a component effect whose deps could re-fire on StrictMode remount
failureExamples: logRun invoked inside useEffect(() => {...}, [lastRun]), firing twice under StrictMode
Counter/log logic in the render body, doubling under StrictMode's double render
logRun in a mount effect, logging on every remount

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is double or spurious logging because logRun was wired to a useEffect on lastRun instead of the dispatch flow — move the logRun call to sit directly beside each of the three post-dispatch setLastRun calls inside handleRun and remove any effect-based logging.

successCriteria: In a local dev build folding, autocomplete responsiveness, and the per-run console log all work as described in the success definition, and npm run build (tsc -b + vite build) still passes.

Add fold gutter and style it for the dark theme: extensionsFor(lang) includes codeFolding() + foldGutter() with foldKeymap in the keymap, and editorTheme contains .cm-foldGutter and .cm-foldPlaceholder rules, so the editor folds/unfolds ranges legibly in JS and TS modes.

Cache global-scope completions off the typing tick: editorCompletions.ts registers a memoized/deferred replacement for the raw scopeCompletionSource(globalThis) that computes the global-scope list once and serves it via validFor.

Log run counter and result after each run: handleRun calls a module-level-counter-backed logRun(result) at exactly the three post-dispatch setLastRun sites, emitting one console.log(`${counter}`, result) per run.
deferred: Item 4 / the 'TS or linter not working when deployed' report — user confirmed it is a false alarm and explicitly excluded.
Wiring @codemirror/lint diagnostics or a linter into the editor — installed but not part of these three improvements.
Rewriting or relocating the TypeScript compile step or the sandbox.worker.ts run pipeline beyond adding the log — the run mechanism itself is not being changed.
Persisting fold state, editor preferences, or the run counter to localStorage / app store — prototype scope is in-memory only.
Adding a visible in-app run-counter or run-history UI — item 3 targets the browser console only.
Piping sandbox user-code console.log output into the browser console or a custom console panel — out of scope.
A formal performance benchmark harness or profiling report for autocomplete latency — light verification only at the prototype bar.
New automated test suites for folding, the completion wrapper, or the run log — user marked tests optional.
Broader editor features (multi-cursor config, minimap, bracket-pair colorization, search panel, linting gutter) not named in the three items.
Refactoring CodeEditor.tsx's ~881-line structure beyond what these changes require.
Changing completion content/ranking quality or adding new completion sources — only the execution model is being optimized.
Upgrading CodeMirror or related package versions.
Moving the TypeScript LanguageService completion source into a Web Worker — discovery shows it is already async/off the typing tick and a worker port exceeds the prototype bar (YAGNI gate 2/3).
Introducing a Compartment or pluggable completion-backend abstraction in CodeEditor.tsx — reconfigure already rebuilds the extension list and there is only one backend (YAGNI gate 3).
